candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; initiate emergency response systems, coordinate interprofessional care, and implement established protocols for rapidly changing client conditions
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — activation of a standardized postpartum hemorrhage response protocol
candidate.educational_objective: Activate an established obstetric hemorrhage protocol promptly when postpartum hemorrhage is recognized so assessment, resuscitation, treatment, and escalation occur in a coordinated manner while the cause is evaluated.

options.A: Activate the standardized hemorrhage protocol promptly so the interprofessional team can begin the predefined assessment, resuscitation, treatment, and escalation process without waiting for deterioration.
options.B: Wait for the attending clinician to arrive before initiating the facility’s hemorrhage response because nurses should not activate standardized emergency protocols.
options.C: Use the hemorrhage protocol only after cesarean birth because standardized postpartum hemorrhage response does not apply after vaginal delivery.
options.D: Delay protocol activation until the exact cause of bleeding is fully confirmed because coordinated response should begin only after a definitive diagnosis.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. ACOG’s postpartum hemorrhage guidance emphasizes rapid recognition, evaluation, treatment, and implementation of standardized hemorrhage bundles, policies, guidelines, and algorithms to support coordinated obstetric care. A client with heavy postpartum bleeding and hypovolemic signs should therefore trigger the facility’s established response promptly while evaluation of the cause continues. B creates an unsafe delay in a time-sensitive emergency. C is false because postpartum hemorrhage can occur after any birth route. D is incorrect because stabilization and coordinated response should not be postponed until every etiologic detail is known.
candidate.source_claim_supported: ACOG supports standardized obstetric hemorrhage bundles/protocols to enable prompt, coordinated evaluation and management of postpartum hemorrhage rather than delaying response until deterioration or complete etiologic confirmation.
candidate.source_locator: Practice Bulletin abstract and purpose — postpartum hemorrhage requires evaluation, prevention, and management; obstetric care providers should implement standardized bundles of care, including policies, guidelines, and algorithms, for postpartum hemorrhage management; bulletin includes acute medical management framework
candidate.source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
candidate.source_version_date: Practice Bulletin reaffirmed 2024; July 2025 Clinical Practice Update; accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A postpartum client develops heavy bleeding with signs of hypovolemia. The nurse recognizes postpartum hemorrhage and the facility has an established obstetric hemorrhage response protocol. Which action is most appropriate?
